name: Can I expand a bathroom into an adjacent bedroom or closet in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: Can I take space from a bedroom, closet, or hallway to expand a bathroom in my house?
mainEntity.text: Can I take space from a bedroom, closet, or hallway to expand a bathroom in my house?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, many bathroom expansions in Los Angeles-area homes are created by borrowing space from a nearby closet, hallway, or small bedroom. This is one of the most common ways to improve a cramped bathroom without adding new exterior square footage. The feasibility depends on whether the wall can be moved, how far plumbing must shift, and whether the remaining room still has practical value. In older homes, especially those with small compartmentalized rooms, converting a closet or part of a bedroom can create a much better primary bath layout. The tradeoff is that the adjacent room may lose storage or usability, so the design should be evaluated as a whole-house decision. Before construction, the space should be measured carefully and a conceptual floor plan should show fixture placement, door swings, ventilation, and traffic flow. If the expansion involves structural walls or changes to plumbing and electrical systems, planning becomes even more important. A good design will improve the bathroom without creating a worse problem somewhere else.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, bathroom expansions often use space from an adjacent closet, hallway, or small bedroom, as long as the new layout works structurally and code requirements are met. The main issues are load-bearing walls, plumbing relocation, ventilation, and making sure the remaining room still functions properly.
